incident-bot: INCIDENT: alert threshold changed for route /api/generate from 200ms -> 350ms at 2024-11-13T03:47:02Z. Source: infra-slo-adjuster. Paging still enabled.
Alex P: Whoa — did we opt to relax latency alert? Who signed off on this? @Maya R you're primary tonight, were you looped in?
Maya R: Yep, saw the bot. Product requested a temporary suppression to reduce noise during a batch rollout. We agreed to a short window but we should be explicit in handoff. I'm primary, @Jordan K is secondary.
Jordan K: Confirmed secondary. I'm going to open a quick bridge: #incident-bridge-1719004822. Drop in if you want to triage live.
Samir: Heads up — CS flagged AcmePay with elevated retries and token cost. Correlated p95/p99 latency increase on our telemetry around the same time. Marking P1 for customer impact.
Kevin L: On it. Looking at logs now. Note: the suppression adjusted only the latency alert, error-rate and 5xx pages still active. We should add an explicit expire time and record owners for the window.
Alex P: Please paste the runbook + exact commands you used to change the threshold so handoff is clean. Also update PagerDuty note so secondary knows to escalate.
Maya R: Added runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/slo-threshold-change (see section 'temporary_thresholds' -> rollback & verify). Quick commands I used:
```
# verify current threshold
curl -sS "https://metrics/api/v1/query?query=slo_latency_threshold{route=\"/api/generate\"}"
# set temporary threshold (ops-admin)
redwoodctl config set slo.threshold.route:/api/generate 350 --until=2024-11-13T04:30:00Z
```
Jordan K: Also left a PagerDuty annotation: "Suppress noisy latency alerts during batch rollout" and set owner = Maya R. PD won't auto-resolve unless we toggle auto-unset; left manual for now.
Samir: CS update: AcmePay reporting increased costs due to retries. I opened a hotfix PR to limit spikes per-tenant: https://git.internal/r/redwood/retries/PR-489 — if we can canary this, might reduce immediate impact.
Kevin L: I can roll canary patch. Plan: roll to canary, watch p95 and error-rate for 15m, then promote. Adding a one-liner to runbook for deploy ops: `kubectl -n inference patch deployment router -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"slo-temporary":"true"}}}}}'`
Alex P: :thumbsup: Good. For shift handoff I'll copy these notes and call out owners explicitly. Maya primary until 04:30 UTC, Jordan secondary, Kevin escalation for deploys, Samir customer comms.
Maya R: Leaving a short checklist in #shift-handoffs as well:
```
- Primary: Maya R
- Secondary: Jordan K
- Escalation: Kevin L (deploys), Samir (customer comms)
- SLO change: /api/generate latency 200->350ms until 04:30 UTC
- Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/slo-threshold-change
- PagerDuty note: 'temp suppression for batch rollout'
```
Jordan K: I'll standby for any PD pages. If I get paged I'll start the bridge and ping @exec-sre + send a short status to leadership channel.
incident-bot: Reminder: scheduled auto-revert in 00:42:58. Use `redwoodctl config unset slo.threshold.route:/api/generate` to revert early if rollout stabilizes.
Alex P: Thanks all. I'll hand this off at 03:50 UTC with these notes. If anything degrades we escalate to SEV. /me signs off for now.
